extracted.intended_audience: Prospective authors and contributors to The Mathematical Intelligencer (mathematicians, historians of mathematics, and the wider intellectual community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors preparing submissions to The Mathematical Intelligencer: the journal seeks engaging, informal expository and cultural pieces about mathematics, mathematicians, and related history and culture, and also accepts creative works that connect math with broader cultural themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: topics published
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes articles about mathematics, about mathematicians, and about the history and culture of mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style: engaging, informal prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Written in an engaging, informal style
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Our pages inform and entertain a broad audience of mathematicians and the wider intellectual community; pieces should aim to be accessible and entertaining rather than highly technical research reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience: broad mathematical and intellectual community
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform and entertain a broad audience of mathematicians and the wider intellectual community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepts expository articles on all kinds of mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: We welcome expository articles on all kinds of mathematics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expository pieces should clarify and communicate mathematical ideas rather than present dense original research; exposition across any mathematical area is welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content: portray diversity of mathematical communities and thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles that portray the diversity of mathematical communities and mathematical thought
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pieces highlighting varied perspectives, underrepresented groups, or differing modes of mathematical practice are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on emergent mathematical communities worldwide
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergent mathematical communities around the world
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal encourages submissions that illuminate new or developing mathematical communities and their practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary and cultural relations
rubrics_metrics.description: New interdisciplinary trends, and relations between mathematics and other areas of culture
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions connecting mathematics to other disciplines or to broader cultural topics — including education, arts, history, and society — are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcomes humor and creative forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor is welcome, as are puzzles, poetry, fiction, and art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative, playful, and nontraditional formats that engage readers (e.g., puzzles, mathematical poetry, short fiction, visual art) are explicitly invited alongside expository essays.
